articles.title: Model releases should leave a public evidence trail
articles.author: Global AI News Editorial Desk

content_type_status.rationale: The completed draft was checked against the assigned editorial form.

content.dek: A release should remain understandable after the launch page changes: preserve dates, model identifiers, evaluation context, availability, and revisions.

body.heading: A launch is an event; a record is a system
paragraphs: Model releases now travel through several documents: an announcement, a technical card, API documentation, product access pages, and cloud or partner listings. These pages answer different questions and may be updated at different times. A durable public record should connect them without pretending that they are the same source or that availability proves performance.

The September 2026 model archive in this project shows why. OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol/Luna release page describes product positioning and provider-run benchmarks. Anthropic’s Sonnet 5.5 system card records evaluation coverage and omissions. Google’s Gemini 3.8 Flash card documents modalities and context. xAI’s Grok 4.7 card names external evaluators for selected tests and notes benchmark-version changes. AWS’s captured Bedrock page lists Grok 4.7 availability, but its publication date is not visible; it records a hosting path, not an independent model evaluation. Each document is useful for a different part of the release. [@openai-gpt6-sol-luna-2026] [@anthropic-sonnet55-system-card-2026] [@gemini38-flash-card-2026] [@grok47-model-card-2026] [@aws-grok47-bedrock-2026]

cells: Announcement
Publication date, stated claims, and links to technical documents
Shows what the provider said at launch
Model identity
Stable model ID, checkpoint or revision, API version
Connects an evaluation to an accessible system
Evaluation card
Tasks, methods, tools, trial counts, exclusions, and limitations
Makes performance claims interpretable
Access record
API, product, region, pricing, and eligibility at a stated date
Separates availability from capability
Change log
Updated model, terms, tests, and documentation
Prevents later pages from silently rewriting history
Independent coverage
Reporting date and attributed claims
Adds context without being mistaken for a benchmark

body.heading: Preserve the difference between documents
paragraphs: A release page can make comparative claims that a model card later bounds to a task, effort setting, or test checkpoint. An API page can change a model ID or price after the announcement. A cloud provider can make a model available through its own service without validating the model’s results. Readers need a dated map from claim to evidence.

Independent reporting helps establish timing and commercial context. Reuters’ reporting on Anthropic’s release, for example, can corroborate when the launch happened and what the company announced; it does not turn Anthropic’s benchmark result into an independent finding. The same boundary applies to reporting about OpenAI and xAI: the source of the test result remains the organization that ran or published it. [@reuters-sonnet55-2026] [@reuters-gpt6-sol-luna-2026] [@decrypt-grok47-2026]

The original model-card research proposal argues for documentation of intended use, performance conditions, and evaluation procedures. A public evidence trail extends that idea over time. The record should preserve prior versions, state what changed, and link a result to the model and endpoint that produced it. The card documents the evaluation; the release ledger documents when and where the model could be obtained. [@model-card-paper-2019]

body.heading: Make change visible instead of silently updating the page
paragraphs: A provider should keep a stable identifier and record the date of each change to weights, context limits, safety filters, pricing, or evaluation methods. If a product endpoint serves a changing model behind a stable name, the provider should disclose that behavior and give users a way to pin or identify revisions where possible. If the page is corrected, the previous claim should remain in an archive with the correction date.

The public record should also state what is unknown. If no external assessment exists, say so. If an evaluator could not inspect weights or training data, disclose that. If a model card covers only one language, task family, or safety domain, make the boundary visible. Silence is not evidence of a pass.

This approach protects against two opposite mistakes. A reader should not treat a marketing claim as independent proof; a provider should not be accused of hiding evidence merely because a public page is incomplete. A versioned record makes both critique and correction more precise.

body.heading: A release trail is infrastructure for accountability
paragraphs: Researchers need to reproduce or challenge evaluations. Journalists need to verify dates and attribution. Customers need to know which model, terms, and region they are buying. Public agencies need a clear record of what vendors represented when a system was procured. Those are different use cases, but they all benefit from stable source links and dated changes.

The proposal is modest: every model release should have a dated index page linking to the announcement, model or system card, API documentation, pricing and access terms, known limitations, independent evaluations, and a revision log. Each linked document should retain its publication date and prior versions. This does not certify the model. It preserves the evidence needed to judge it later.

A change log should use separate dated entries for model revisions, evaluation updates, pricing or terms changes, and new access routes. Each entry should say whether it corrects an earlier statement or records a new event, link the affected document, and identify what changed. Keep announcement, publication, and availability dates intact when a page is updated; if a version or effective date is not stated, leave it unknown instead of inferring one from the latest page.
The index should also show when each source was last retrieved and whether its details are confirmed, unknown, or superseded.
**Bottom line:** A release should leave a connected, versioned evidence trail that separates product claims, evaluation, availability, and independent reporting.
**Why it matters:** When pages change or endpoints update, readers can lose the basis for a claim that once shaped a decision.

**Key takeaways:** Treat announcement, card, API docs, and hosting notice as distinct records. Tie benchmarks to the tested version and method. Date pricing, model access, region, and terms separately from launch claims. Preserve corrections and prior documents. Mark missing evaluations as unknown rather than implying a pass.
**What changes:** Model providers and publishers should maintain a stable release index with dated evidence links and a change log.
